seoTitle: Free CSS 3D Box-Shadow Generator with Preview
metaDescription: Build 3D box-shadow CSS: stepped extrusion, long shadow, realistic layered elevation or hard retro offset. Live preview. Free, in your browser.
intro: Create multi-layer box-shadows that look three-dimensional: stepped extrusion, long flat shadow, smooth realistic elevation or a hard retro offset, with colour, depth and direction controls.
why:
A single box-shadow gives a soft blur, but depth effects need many layers. A chunky 3D button is a stack of one-pixel steps in the same direction, a long shadow runs diagonally across the page, and a realistic card shadow is made of several soft layers that grow together. Writing twenty values by hand and keeping them consistent is not fun.

This generator builds the stack from a handful of settings: style, shadow and face colour, depth, direction as an angle and opacity for layered shadows. The preview is a button-like block so you can judge the effect directly. Copy the CSS when it looks right. The calculation runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely.
howTo: Choose a style: 3D extrude, long shadow, layered realistic or hard retro.
Set the shadow colour, face colour and depth in pixels.
Set the direction in degrees, where 0 points right and 90 points down, and the opacity for layered shadows.
Check the preview and copy the CSS into your stylesheet.

faq.q: Will many shadow layers slow down my page?
faq.a: A handful of layers on a few elements is fine. Very deep extrusions on many animated elements can cost rendering time, so keep the depth modest and test on a low-end phone.
It sets the direction the shadow extends, measured in degrees, with 0 pointing right and 90 pointing down. A 45 degree angle gives the classic bottom-right look.

faq.q: Which style is best for a button?
faq.a: The 3D extrude and hard retro styles read as pressable, since you can shrink the offset on :active to make the button look pushed in. Layered realistic is better suited to cards and panels.
